task.description:
Implement the APPROVED design at src/design/iss0627-lint-handoffs-acknowledgment.md (935 lines, commit 86e7c12, PASSed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR at commit 9183e8b) -- a permanent acknowledgment baseline mechanism for tools/lint_handoffs.py covering H003 (148 BLOCKER), H004 (34 BLOCKER), H005 (5 BLOCKER), H009 (38 MAJOR).

CRITICAL: implement the H009-only key fix EXACTLY as specified -- an H009 finding's key must fold in a stable, sorted fingerprint of later_completed's file paths (join sorted rel paths, per CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's confirmation there's no hash-vs-list ambiguity since paths are already POSIX-normalized once in main()). Get this exactly right -- this is the one part of the design that closes a genuine safety gap (two different orphan situations on the same file with the same COUNT of later-completed steps but different actual steps must NOT collide under the same acknowledgment).

Key implementation points (verify against the actual design file, this is a summary not a substitute for reading all 935 lines):
- Baseline file: tools/lint_handoffs.baseline.json (new), matching the sibling-file convention of tools/lint_test_isolation.baseline.json and tools/lint_test_tenant_provisioning.baseline.json.
- Header provenance fields: version, generated_at, source, regenerated_by, regeneration_note, plus a reasons map (one shared reason per category: H003/H004/H005/H009, referencing ISS-0627's already-written root-cause text -- do not write 225 individual reasons).
- Per-finding entries keyed by severity|code|path|message (H003/H004/H005) or severity|code|path|message|<sorted-later-completed-fingerprint> (H009 only).
- A ONE-TIME GENERATION SCRIPT that imports and calls lint_handoffs.py's EXISTING _lint_parsed_handoff and lint_orphans functions -- do NOT reimplement the H003/H004/H005/H009 predicates a second time, that risks silent drift between the baseline generator and the real linter.
- A new ACKNOWLEDGED bucket in lint_handoffs.py's reporting: excluded from the BLOCKER/MAJOR count that decides exit code, but still individually printed (e.g. '[ACKNOWLEDGED]' prefix) so it never becomes invisible.
- A --no-baseline flag that restores full gating and prints an audit line (e.g. 'Suppressed N issue(s) from baseline' equivalent).
- This baseline mechanism composes as an INDEPENDENT SECOND GATE after the existing --changed mode's preexisting_file_finding_codes/preexisting_run_finding_codes logic from GH-594 -- do not merge them into one mechanism, they answer different questions.
- Implement all 5 mutation-checkable test specs from design section 7 (likely as a selftest subcommand or extension of the existing test surface -- check whether lint_handoffs.py already has a selftest pattern or whether this needs its own, following the same convention tools/repair_handoff_bookkeeping.py established in GH-594).

SEQUENCE:
1. Implement the mechanism in tools/lint_handoffs.py plus the new one-time generation script (design section 2 -- check its exact proposed filename/location).
2. Run whatever selftest/test mechanism the design specifies -- all specs must pass against synthetic fixtures BEFORE touching the real baseline file.
3. Run the generation script against the REAL corpus to produce the actual tools/lint_handoffs.baseline.json with ~225 entries. Sanity-check the counts (148 H003 + 34 H004 + 5 H005 + 38 H009 = 225) before committing.
4. Run `python tools/lint_handoffs.py` (full corpus, no flags) and confirm: BLOCKER count drops by 148+34+5=187 (H003/H004/H005 fully acknowledged), MAJOR count drops by 38 (H009 fully acknowledged), and an ACKNOWLEDGED bucket now shows 225 entries -- these findings must still be individually visible in the output, just not gating.
5. Run `python tools/lint_handoffs.py --no-baseline` and confirm full gating is restored (counts back to pre-baseline levels).
6. Run `python tools/lint_handoffs.py --changed` and confirm it still works correctly and independently of the new baseline mechanism (GH-594's logic must be untouched).
7. Confirm this run's own handoff files remain unaffected/clean.
acceptance_criteria: H009 key correctly folds in sorted later_completed fingerprint
Generation script reuses _lint_parsed_handoff/lint_orphans, does not reimplement predicates
Full-corpus lint_handoffs.py run shows ACKNOWLEDGED bucket with 225 entries, BLOCKER/MAJOR reduced accordingly
--changed mode still works correctly, independent of new mechanism
This run's own handoff files unaffected

result.summary: Implemented the ISS-0627/GH-596 permanent-acknowledgment baseline mechanism for tools/lint_handoffs.py per src/design/iss0627-lint-handoffs-acknowledgment.md, covering H003 (148 BLOCKER), H004 (34 BLOCKER), H005 (5 BLOCKER), H009 (38 MAJOR). New tools/generate_lint_handoffs_baseline.py generation script reuses lint_handoffs.py's own _lint_parsed_handoff and lint_orphans (via a new optional capture kwarg) rather than reimplementing the detection predicates. H009's matching_key folds in a sorted fingerprint of later_completed's file paths (H009 only) to close the message-only-key collision gap identified in design section 0.2 -- verified via TS-BASELINE-03 against a synthetic fixture mirroring that exact scenario. Generated the real baseline: 225 entries (148 H003 + 34 H004 + 5 H005 + 38 H009), matching the design's expected counts exactly. Added --baseline/--no-baseline CLI flags and an ACKNOWLEDGED bucket to lint_handoffs.py's main() (individually printed, excluded only from the BLOCKER/MAJOR exit-code count), plus a new `selftest` subcommand on both scripts covering all 5 mutation-checkable test specs from design section 7. Composes as an independent second gate after --changed mode's existing preexisting_file_finding_codes/preexisting_run_finding_codes logic (GH-594) -- neither mechanism is aware of the other.
